metadata.title: Kriegman, Blackiston, Levin & Bongard (2020) PNAS 117:1853-1859 & Kriegman et al. (2021) PNAS 118:e2112672118 — Voxel Spring-Lattice Biomechanics, Age-Fitness Pareto Optimization (AFPO), & Kinematic Self-Replication in Xenopus laevis Biobots (Xenobots)

sources.citation: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J (2020). A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 117(4):1853-1859.
Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J (2021). Kinematic self-replication in reconfigurable organisms. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 118(49):e2112672118.
Blackiston D, Lederer E, Kriegman S, Garnier S, Bongard J, Levin M (2021). A cellular platform for the development of synthetic living machines. Science Robotics 6(52):eabf1571.
Cheney N, MacCurdy R, Clune J, Lipson H (2013). Unshackling evolution: evolving soft robots with multiple materials and a powerful generative encoding. Proceedings of GECCO 2013, pp. 167-174.

xenopus_biobot_specimen.species: Xenopus laevis (African clawed frog reconfigurable organism / Xenobot micro-sculpted from blastula animal-cap ectoderm progenitors and red-fluorescent contractile cardiac progenitor tissue)

governing_equations.section: Kriegman et al. (2020) PNAS 117:1853-1859 SI Appendix S1-S3 (VoxCAD / CPPN-AFPO) & Kriegman et al. (2021) PNAS 118:e2112672118 Figs. 1-4
governing_equations.voxel_rest_length_actuation: L_{ij}(t) = L_{ij,0} * (1 + epsilon_act * a_ij * sin(2 * pi * f_act * t + phi_{ij}))
governing_equations.voxel_spring_lattice_dynamics: m_i * d^2x_i/dt^2 + c_damp * dx_i/dt = sum_{j in N(i)} k_{ij} * (||x_j - x_i|| - L_{ij}(t)) * (x_j - x_i)/||x_j - x_i|| + F_ground(x_i, dx_i/dt)
governing_equations.substrate_friction_ratchet: F_{ground,x}(x_i, v_i) = -mu_k(v_{i,x}) * N_i * sign(v_{i,x}), where N_i = max(0, -k_g * y_i) for y_i < 0
governing_equations.robustness_transferability_filter: F_robust(G) = E_{phi ~ U(-pi, pi)} [ F(G, phi) ], filtering out phase-fragile designs that fail under biological cardiomyocyte phase noise
governing_equations.laceration_regeneration_ode: dr_wound/dt = -k_heal * r_wound * (1 - r_wound / r_crit), restoring structural spring connectivity across mechanical incisions
governing_equations.kinematic_self_replication_rate: dN_pile/dt = eta_sweep(theta_mouth) * v_orbit * rho_free * W_mouth, forming self-sustaining daughter spheroids when N_pile >= N_thresh (C-shaped Pac-Man morphology, theta_mouth ~ 55-75 deg)

evolved_ventral_biped.label: AFPO-Evolved Ventral-Concavity Bipedal Xenobot (Layered Ventral Cardiac + Dorsal Passive Ectoderm)
evolved_ventral_biped.kriegman_reference: Kriegman et al. (2020) Fig. 1 & Fig. 2: Ventral concavity creates anterior/posterior contact legs; ventral contractile cardiac layer (red) working against dorsal passive ectoderm (cyan/tan) generates net forward displacement F = 1.95 body lengths per 10 s.

phase_randomized_transfer_test.label: Transferability Filter Under Desynchronized Cardiac Phase Noise (phi_i ~ U[-pi, pi])
phase_randomized_transfer_test.kriegman_reference: Kriegman et al. (2020) Fig. 2C-E: Real Xenopus cardiomyocytes contract without centralized neural pacing; contiguous ventral cardiac layers retain >65% forward displacement under random phase noise, whereas scattered/checkerboard designs collapse.

inverted_dorsal_up_control.label: Inverted Dorsal-Side-Down Negative Control (Flipped 180 deg onto Smooth Dorsal Back)
inverted_dorsal_up_control.kriegman_reference: Kriegman et al. (2020) Fig. 3C-D: Flipping the evolved Xenobot upside down onto its convex dorsal ectoderm removes substrate leg ratchet asymmetry, collapsing net displacement to <0.18 body lengths.

mechanical_laceration_regeneration.label: Mechanical Laceration & Autonomous Wound Closure (~50% Hinge Incision Recovery)
mechanical_laceration_regeneration.kriegman_reference: Kriegman et al. (2020) Fig. 5: Xenobots cut nearly in half (~50% body width laceration) autonomously close the wound via tissue contractility/adhesion and recover >85% of pre-injury forward velocity.

pacman_kinematic_self_replication.label: C-Shaped ('Pac-Man') Kinematic Self-Replication vs Spherical Control (Kriegman et al. 2021)
pacman_kinematic_self_replication.kriegman_reference: Kriegman et al. (2021) PNAS Fig. 1-3: AI-designed C-shaped torus/concavity parent Xenobots sweep dissociated stem cells into compacted multi-generational daughter spheroids (3-4 generations vs 1-2 for un-sculpted spheres, >2.4x daughter yield).
